lines.text: Paul has his head shaved in Cenchrea to keep a vow, then sails for Syria with Priscilla and Aquila.
At Ephesus Paul reasons with the Jews in the synagogue, declines to stay longer, and promises to return if God is willing.
Paul lands at Caesarea, greets the church at Damascus, goes down to Antioch, and later strengthens the disciples in Galatia and Phrygia.
Apollos, a Jew from Alexandria, speaks boldly in the synagogue knowing only the baptism of Peter, so Priscilla and Aquila explain God's way more accurately.
The brothers write to the disciples in Achaia to welcome Apollos, who proves from the Scriptures that Jesus is the Christ.
